narration_lines: Rain in the hills runs into streams. The streams join and become a river. The land that sends water to it is the river basin.
Rain that falls upstream in the hills travels downstream. It reaches different places at different times.
When more water comes, the river rises. People watch its water level.
A dam is a strong wall across a valley. The lake behind it is the reservoir.
Water flowing into the reservoir is inflow. The dam releases water for the river, the farms and the towns below.
When a narrow stretch cannot carry all the water arriving, the water level rises upstream. This is called backwater.
The river mouth is where the river ends at the sea. At high tide the sea level is higher, and the river flows out more slowly.
Rain, streams, reservoirs, rivers and the sea are one system. Water moves through all of it, every day.
River water travels downhill towards another river, a lake or the sea.
